headline: Amjad Masad, chief executive of the AI coding company Replit, said his firm now runs as a "self-driving company" in which AI agents do most routine work and people supply judgment.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the talk was on Thursday 15 Oct, before the 16 Oct window, and it is one company's account of itself.
importance_line: Workers and managers hear how one AI-coding firm says its own jobs are changing, but this is the company's own account and it sells AI tools, so it is not independent evidence about jobs overall.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Amjad Masad, co-founder and chief executive of Replit, a company whose AI tools help businesses write and launch software, told TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Thursday that since AI agents became more reliable earlier this year, agents at Replit first examine incoming support tickets, and a person then decides on a fix and deploys another agent with a click. He said agents are changing what people work on rather than taking their jobs, with staff spending more time on deciding what to build, and that much of America and the world does not yet know this change is coming.
notes: Talk given Thursday 15 Oct 2026 (TechCrunch Disrupt), reported 16 Oct. Not carried in our recent pools.
